articles.content: On Nov. 6, Titus Hassan Malika stood with his classmates and received his diploma — a quiet but powerful moment marking the end of a long, difficult road. The Sudanese Christian, who fled violence and persecution in his homeland, had received support from International Christian Concern (ICC). With God’s help, what once seemed impossible had become reality. “The support I received from ICC is a dream come true,” Malika said. “I never imagined that someone would stand with me for so many years, believing in my future when I could barely see it myself. This graduation is not only my achievement — it is the fruit of their faithfulness and God’s provision.” Titus grew up in Sudan, where following Jesus grew increasingly dangerous . As pressure on Christian communities intensified amid conflict and targeted hostility, he was forced to leave everything behind. With little more than his faith, he crossed into Kenya as a refugee, carrying the weight of loss, uncertainty, and the hope that God still had a future for him. By His Side In 2023, ICC stepped into that uncertainty. Through consistent support, practical help, encouragement, and the means to continue his studies, we walked with Titus through years of hardship. The path was not easy. He faced the daily challenges of life, the lingering trauma of persecution, and the enduring discipline of education while far from home. Yet he pressed on. “Jesus Christ has been the center of my life from the day I fled Sudan until this moment,” he said. “When I had no home, he was my shelter. When fear tried to silence me, he gave me courage. Every step of this journey has been possible only because he walked with me and never left me alone.” As he steps into his next chapter, Titus carries both a Bachelor’s degree in business administration and management, as well as a testimony that God can bring beauty from ashes, and that the Body of Christ, when it stands with the persecuted, can help rewrite a life marked by suffering into one marked by grace. “I give thanks to God for ICC, for they have been the hands and feet of Christ to me,” he said. “As it is written, ‘And my God will meet all your needs according to the riches of his glory in Christ Jesus’ (Philippians 4:19). Truly, the Lord has done this. May he continue to bless those who have poured out their lives so that I could stand here today.” To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . For interviews, please email us . To support ICC’s work around the world, please give to our Where Most Needed Fund . The post The Journey Through Persecution to Graduation first appeared on International Christian Concern .

由于在冲突和有目标的敌意中,对基督教社区的压力加剧,他被迫留下一切。 他带着微乎其微的信仰,以难民身份越境进入肯尼亚,背负着损失,不确定性的重担,希望上帝仍然有他的未来. 在他的身边 2023年,国际商会介入了这种不确定性。

被恩典冲动 他说,“我为国际刑事法院感谢上帝,因为他们是基督的手脚。” " 上面写道: " 我 的 神 、 也 必 照 他 在 基督 耶穌 中 的 丰盛 、 满足 你 一切 的 需要 " ( 菲利浦 4: 19) 。 真的,上帝已经这样做了。

愿他继续保佑那些倾注生命的人,以便我今天能够站在这里。” 阅读更多新闻, 请给我们发电子邮件 支持电算中心在世界各地的工作, 文章《透过迫害到毕业的旅程》首次出现在国际基督教关注上。

articles.title_zh: 穆斯林枪手在高原袭击中杀死6人后没有逮捕
articles.content: Suspected Muslim Gunmen killed at least six people, including a Nigerian soldier, in separate attacks on communities in Plateau state, Nigeria. The attacks occurred on Sunday night, Nov. 8, in Bel village, Sho community, Barkin Ladi Local Government Area (LGA), and Lakas community in Panyam, near the Mangu-Pankshin border in Mangu LGA. Four people, including three civilians and a soldier, were reportedly killed when gunmen stormed Bel village at about 9 p.m. and opened fire. A resident of Bel village, Bulus Bot, who confirmed the attack to International Christian Concern (ICC), said several people also sustained gunshot injuries. The attack forced residents to seek safety as gunfire rang through the community. He said the attackers are Islamic Fulani herders who want to take over their land. Rwang Tengwong, publicity secretary of the Berom Youth Moulders Association (BYM), confirmed the killings and identified three of the civilian victims as Emmanuel Pam Dachung, 15; Joseph Gyang, 28; and Emmanuel Yohanna, 32. The soldier has not been publicly identified. According to a six-year study conducted by the Observatory for Religious Freedom in Africa (ORFA), Islamic Fulani militias are by far the deadliest persecutors of Christians in Nigeria. The network of militias is responsible for four times more civilian deaths than the two prominent Islamic terror organizations, Boko Haram and Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP), combined. The study’s findings challenge the commonly held belief that the two organized terror groups kill the larger number of Christians, highlighting the Fulani network’s expanded efforts to target Christians. A Second Attack Two additional people were reportedly killed in a separate attack on the Lakas community in Panyam, bringing the reported death toll from the two incidents to at least six. “Muslim Fulani stopped us from going to the farm to harvest our crops, and we are now afraid to go to the church to worship,” Mathias said. “Nigerian authorities failed to protect us.” Tengwong told ICC that no arrests had been made following either attack. He specifically accused the Nigerian Army of failing to apprehend any of the suspected Fulani attackers. Tengwong condemned the killings and called on security agencies to identify and arrest those responsible, warning that the failure to apprehend attackers could leave surrounding communities exposed to further violence. Residents and eyewitnesses alleged that Fulani extremists carried out the attacks, targeting predominantly Christian communities. Some residents described the assaults as part of a pattern of violence aimed at taking over ancestral lands and forcing indigenous populations from their communities. These allegations could not be independently verified. The latest attacks add to continuing reports of armed assaults against rural communities in Plateau, particularly in Barkin Ladi, Bassa, Riyom, and Mangu local government areas, where Christian farming communities have repeatedly reported killings, destruction of property, displacement, and threats to their livelihoods. To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . For interviews, please email us . To support ICC’s work around the world, please give to our Where Most Needed Fund . The post No Arrests After Muslim Gunmen Kill 6 in Plateau Attacks first appeared on International Christian Concern .

被怀疑的穆斯林枪手在分别袭击尼日利亚高原州社区时至少杀害了六人,包括一名尼日利亚士兵. 袭击发生在星期天晚上11月8日,地点在Sho社区Bel村、Barkin Ladi地方政府区和Mangu LGAMangu-Pankshin边界附近的Panyam的Lakas社区。

据报,有4人,包括3名平民和1名士兵,在晚上9时左右枪手冲进Bel村并开火时被打死。 Bel村的一名居民Bulus Bot向国际基督教关注组织证实这次袭击,他说,一些人也遭到枪伤。 袭击迫使居民在枪声响彻社区时寻求安全。

他说袭击者是伊斯兰富拉尼牧民,他们想占领他们的土地. 贝罗姆青年穆尔德斯协会(BYM)宣传秘书Rwang Tengwong证实了这些杀人事件,并指认了3名平民受害者:15岁的Emmanuel Pam Dachung;28岁的Joseph Gyang;32岁的Emmanuel Yohanna。 该士兵尚未公开确认身份。

根据非洲宗教自由观察站(ORFA)进行的一项为期六年的研究,伊斯兰富拉尼民兵是尼日利亚基督教徒最致命的迫害者。 民兵网络造成平民死亡的人数是博科圣地和西非伊斯兰国省这两个著名的伊斯兰恐怖组织的四倍。

研究结论质疑人们的普遍看法,即两个有组织的恐怖集团杀害了更多的基督徒,突出了富拉尼网络扩大针对基督徒的努力。 第二次攻击 据报告,在对Panyam的Lakas社区进行的另一次袭击中,又有两人丧生,据报这两起事件的死亡人数至少达6人。

Mathias说:“穆斯林Fulani阻止我们去农场收获作物, “尼日利亚当局未能保护我们。” Tengwong告诉国际刑事法院,在两次袭击之后都没有逮捕任何人。 他具体指责尼日利亚军队没有逮捕任何涉嫌的Fulani袭击者。

Tengwong谴责这些杀人事件,呼吁安全机构查明并逮捕肇事者,并警告说,不逮捕袭击者可能会使周围的社区面临进一步的暴力。 居民和目击者指称,Fulani极端分子进行攻击,攻击目标主要是基督教社区。

一些居民称,这些袭击是旨在夺取祖传土地和强迫土著人口离开其社区的暴力模式的一部分。 这些指控无法独立核实。

最近发生的攻击事件使有关对高原农村社区,特别是Barkin Ladi、Bassa、Riyom和Mangu地方政府地区的农村社区进行武装攻击的不断报道更为严重。 在那里,基督教农耕社区一再报告杀害、毁坏财产、流离失所和威胁其生计。 阅读更多新闻,

articles.title: Making a Difference for Future Generations
articles.source: Wycliffe Bible Translators · 译经故事
articles.summary: See how Bible translation is transforming future generations as communities in Guatemala, Peru, Tanzania and Nigeria gain access to God’s Word in languages they clearly understand.   The post  Making a Difference for Future Generations  appeared first on  Wycliffe .
articles.summary_zh: 了解圣经翻译如何改变后代，因为危地马拉、秘鲁、坦桑尼亚和尼日利亚的社区以他们清楚理解的语言获得神的话语。“Making a Difference for Future Generations”一文首次出现在Wycliffe上。
articles.content: How old were you when you first learned that Jesus loves you? Perhaps you’ve always known it and can’t remember a day when you didn’t know the song “Jesus Loves Me” or couldn’t recite John 3:16 by heart. Maybe you were a teenager and learned about Jesus’ love through a friend or church summer camp. Or were in college and went to a concert where the gospel was clearly articulated. Maybe you were in the trenches of the workforce, and a coworker boldly shared with you about the God who radically changed their life. Regardless of how old you were, each of us who has chosen to follow Jesus has an origin story — a moment in our lives when the knowledge that “Jesus loves me, this I know, for the Bible tells me so” moved from head knowledge to heart belief. And from then on, our lives were transformed forever. This is the truth of the gospel and the power of understanding that Jesus loves you. People around the world are discovering the personal truth of John 3:16 for themselves in a language and format they clearly understand. Explore why understanding that “God so loved the world” transforms entire communities → A Changing Reality Throughout Christian history, the gospel has spread from one community to the next. Stories were told and retold, Scripture was translated, churches were planted, and discipleship deepened as people learned more about Jesus. Bible translation is foundational to all ministries of the church. It fuels evangelism, church planting, discipleship and more. It equips people to move from a blurry picture of who God is to a clear understanding and personal encounter with Jesus as Lord. Through Scripture, people are able to read, hear or see the love of God on display. Just two decades ago, most of the world’s language communities still needed Bible translation work to begin , let alone be completed. But praise God, in the last few years, we’ve seen tremendous progress made, with Bible translation underway in more languages than ever before . While the change in numbers is exciting, what’s more important is what they signify: Every number represents a person who has a story that matters to God. For these communities, the stories of future generations are being completely rewritten as children will now grow up never remembering a day when they didn’t have access to God’s Word in a language and format they clearly understand. That statement bears repeating: There will now be people who never remember a day when they didn’t have access to God’s Word in a language and format they clearly understand. From the first word of Genesis to the last word of Revelation, the Bible tells one incredible story: God’s love for the world and His invitation for people from every nation and language to know Him. Get a glimpse of how God continues writing this story today as more and more people are experiencing the power of His Word. Watch the video → A New Generation Growing Up With God’s Word Let’s take a look at some of the recent communities that are experiencing not only life transformation but generational transformation as they encounter Jesus personally through Scripture. Jakalteko | Guatemala The Jakalteko Bible was dedicated in July 2026 in Guatemala! During the celebration, John 1:1-18 was read aloud — a passage that focuses on Christ, the eternal Word and our Redeemer. Early on, many women in the community memorized Job 19 . Like Job, they had faced various hardships in their lives and identified with his suffering. The book reminded them that God remains in control and that, in the midst of difficult circumstances, their Redeemer will deliver them and comfort them in their pain. Today, they have the full counsel of God’s Word and can now see this Redeemer fulfilled in Jesus in the New Testament. They are overjoyed that the Bible has arrived in the language they were born into! 也许你在劳动力的战壕里, 一个合作者大胆地与你分享上帝 谁彻底改变了他们的生活。 无论你多大,选择跟随耶稣的我们每个人都有一个起源故事——在我们生活中的这一刻,“耶稣爱我,我知道,因为圣经如此告诉我”的知识从头知识转移到心信。

从那时起,我们的生活就永远改变了 这是耶稣爱你的福音和理解的力量的真理. 世界各地的人们正在用他们明白的语言和格式,为自己发现约翰3:16的个人真理.

articles.content: ABSTRACT: Just as the serpent led Adam and Eve into idolatry by reinterpreting God’s good word, so prosperity and word-of-faith preachers are today proclaiming a false and idolatrous gospel. But unlike Adam, African preachers are refusing to stay mute. Recognizing the need for faithful interpretation of Scripture, they have drawn up a statement to help pastors stand against the idolatrous assumptions and teachings of the prosperity gospel and word-of-faith theology. For our ongoing series of feature articles for pastors and Christian leaders, we asked Dieudonné Tamfu (PhD, Southern Baptist Theological Seminary), pastor of Église Baptiste Bethléem and Assistant Professor of Bible and Theology and Director of the Cameroon Extension Site of Bethlehem College and Seminary, to introduce readers to the recently published Africa Statement on the Prosperity Gospel and Word of Faith Theology . Christian leadership is war. When God calls a man to shepherd his flock, he calls him to war against wolves. Satan, the father of lies, and his minions hate the spiritual health of God’s people, wanting nothing more than to lead the people of God from truth to idolatry. The spiritual leaders of God’s flock are called to fight against Satan’s counterfeit gospels by proclaiming the word of God (Ephesians 6:17). When those leaders fall silent, when they fail to preach the sufficiency of Christ alone, they make space for Satan to lead the people of God into idolatry. As John Calvin rightly said, “Those in authority in the church turned over to idols the office of teaching for no other reason than that they themselves were mute.” 1 The muteness of faithful leaders gives voices to idols. Since Genesis 3, the devil has been in the business of poisoning the minds of God’s people with lies. In God’s good garden, the enemy came preaching lies: If God truly loves you, he will give you the fruit from the tree in the middle of the garden. Eve paid close attention while Adam idly stood by, mute. Thus he, his wife, and all his descendants died of the poison of Satan. The world is under the curse of sin because of a failure of leadership. 2 One of Satan’s most deceptive counterfeits plaguing both American and African churches is the prosperity gospel, a false teaching that elevates the idols of health, wealth, and power. David Oyedepo, a strong proponent of the prosperity gospel and word-of-faith theology, says, “Healing is the covenant right of every child of God . . . sickness has no right to feast on your life.” He goes on to proclaim healing over his congregation: “In the name of Jesus, I decree an end to every toil with sickness and disease.” He assures them that faith in Jesus means the end of sickness. 3 As I’ve written elsewhere, this “idolatrous perversion of the gospel” turns Jesus into “a means to God’s full blessings, primarily of health, wealth, and might” in the present life. 4 Its widespread success indicates a failure on the part of so-called shepherds to engage in spiritual warfare by speaking the whole testimony of God’s word. Today, many church leaders in Africa are boldly refusing to remain mute while the “new serpent,” the prosperity gospel and word-of-faith theology, reinterpret God’s goodness as mere material blessings. These bold leaders are now advancing the centrality of the true gospel by the recent publication of the Africa Statement on the Prosperity Gospel and Word of Faith Theology . The present essay introduces the statement, first explaining why it is necessary, then summarizing its main points, and concluding with a warning against the syncretism of prosperity teaching. Hermeneutical Battlefield Our hermeneutics determine whom we hallow, and whom we hallow reinforces our hermeneutics. As it was in the garden, the fight for the people of God is the battle for faithful interpretation of God’s word. 亚伯拉罕:就像蛇通过重新诠释上帝的好言语把亚当和夏娃引向偶像崇拜一样,今天,繁荣和虔诚的传教士正在宣布一个虚假和偶像崇拜的福音。 但与亚当不同,非洲传教士拒绝保持沉默.

他们认识到需要对《圣经》进行忠实的解释,因此起草了一份声明,帮助牧师们反对繁荣福音和信仰神学的偶像主义假设和教义。

为了不断为牧师和基督教领袖发表一系列专题文章,我们请贝瑟莱姆浸信会牧师Dieudonné Tamfu(南方浸信会神学院博士)兼圣经和神学助理教授兼伯利恒学院和神学院喀麦隆扩展场地主任向读者介绍最近发表的《非洲繁荣福音书》。

d 信仰神学之词。 基督教的领导是战争. 当上帝召唤一个人牧羊时,他召唤他与狼作战. 撒旦,谎言之父,他的仆人,痛恨真主的百姓的精神健康,只想把真主的百姓从真理引向以物配主。

神羊的精神领袖们被要求通过宣示上帝之言(以弗所6:17)来对抗撒旦的假福音. 当这些领袖们沉默不语,当他们未能独自宣扬基督的充足性时,他们为撒旦创造了空间,让撒旦带领上帝的百姓进入偶像崇拜.

正如约翰·加尔文正确指出的那样 , “ 那些在教会中掌权的人把教职者交给偶像,除了他们自己是哑巴之外没有其他理由。 ” 页:1 忠实领导人的哑巴给偶像带来声音. 自创世纪3以来,恶魔一直在用谎言毒害上帝人民的思想。

在真主的好园圃里,敌人来传谣:如果真主真的爱你,他就把园圃中央树上的果实赏赐你。 夏娃在亚当袖手旁观时,一直密切关注,哑巴. 于是他妻子和子孙都死于撒旦的毒药. 世界因为领导力的失败而受到罪恶的诅咒.

2 撒旦最欺骗性的假象之一, 是繁荣的福音, 大卫·奥耶德波是繁荣福音和信仰神学的坚定支持者,他说,“治愈是上帝每个儿童的盟约权利。

疾病没有权利用餐。 他说:我奉耶稣之名,命令结束每一次病痛。 他向他们保证,对耶稣的信仰意味着疾病的结束.

3 正如我在别处所写的那样,这种 " 对福音的盲目歪曲 " 使耶稣在现今生活中成为 " 充分保佑上帝的手段,主要是健康、财富和力量的手段 " 。 4 它的广泛成功表明,所谓的牧羊人没有通过说出神话的全部证据而参与精神战争。

今天,非洲许多教会领袖大胆地拒绝保持沉默,而“新蛇 ” 、 繁荣的福音和信仰的神学则将上帝的善良重新解释为仅仅是物质上的祝福。 这些大胆的领导人最近发表了《关于繁荣福音和信仰神话的非洲声明》,推动真正的福音的中心地位。

本篇论文介绍了这一陈述,首先解释了为什么有必要,然后总结了其要点,最后警告大家不要同时进行繁荣教学。 赫梅纽奇战地 我们的修炼决定了我们向谁致敬,我们向谁致敬加强了我们的修炼。

在花园里,为上帝的人民而战,就是为忠实地解释上帝的话而战。 圣经解释可以创造偶像,也可以培养爱和崇拜一个真正的上帝. 如果我们的翻译技巧发热

对在塞内加尔服务的国际传教委员会传教士卡森·韦斯特来说,奥运会是一个独特的机会,不仅可以让游客接受福音,还可以动员当地教会在奥运会火焰熄灭很久后,在福音仪式中发挥更积极的作用。
articles.title_zh: IMB传教士到位，准备鼓励塞内加尔教会开展青年奥运会外展活动
articles.content: A Senegalese Christian shares the gospel with event volunteers during the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar. IMB Photo As athletes and spectators from around the world fill the streets of Senegal for the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, missionaries and local believers are praying the event will leave behind more than medals and memories. For Carson West, an International Mission Board missionary serving in Senegal, the Games represent a unique opportunity not only to engage visitors with the gospel but also to mobilize local churches to take a more active role in evangelism long after the Olympic flame is extinguished. “This is the first Olympic event ever held on the continent of Africa,” West said. “For us, it was an opportunity to ask, ‘What are we going to do with this?’” The Youth Olympic Games, which began Oct. 31 and end Nov. 13, are taking place across three host cities: Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly. Event organizers expect nearly 2,700 athletes, ages 14-17, to participate in 35 sports and represent more than 200 delegations. The Games have drawn a million spectators, and West reported more than 6,000 event volunteers are staffing all the venues. With so many people gathering in Senegal, West and his team concentrated on preparing Senegalese churches for evangelistic opportunities. “We could run and hide, or we could do this thing,” West said, recalling an early conversation with teammates. “We decided we were going to do this thing.” The 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal, is the first Olympic event held on the continent of Africa. IMB Photo West serves as team leader for IMB work in Senegal, where ministry efforts focus on three areas: gospel engagement, church advancement and community development. The Youth Olympic outreach naturally aligns with the first two priorities. “Our approach has been to mobilize the local church,” he said. “This is their backyard.” Instead of relying on a large influx of international volunteers, though there is one volunteer team from the United States serving, the strategy has centered on equipping local believers. Senegal has four Baptist churches in the greater Dakar area. Many leaders representing the congregations, as well as other ministry partners, participated in evangelism training designed specifically for the Games. Church leaders and ministry partners in Senegal participate in an evangelism training session specifically designed to share the gospel during the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar. IMB Photo A key outreach method involves trading commemorative pins, a familiar Olympic tradition. Volunteers use the exchange as a natural conversation starter before offering gospel-centered materials. Each pin is accompanied by a card featuring a QR code connected to a digital engagement platform adapted from previous Olympic and World Cup outreaches. Visitors who scan the code are directed to online resources and can connect with trained digital responders. Experienced volunteers in the U.S. are helping provide follow-up conversations. “We’re building on strategies that have been used effectively in previous Olympic Games,” West said. “It’s an easy, non-intimidating way to start gospel conversations.” Trading commemorative pins is an Olympic tradition. Volunteers use these pins to start gospel-driven conversations during the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar. Each pin is accompanied by a card featuring a QR code that connects people to trained digital responders. IMB Photo The effort extends beyond Dakar. IMB teams and church partners are positioned in each of the three host cities. An IMB team, which includes three global missionary partners, is helping coordinate outreach efforts in Diamniadio, and an IMB team along with a Baptist church is organizing efforts in Saly. West believes the greatest potential impact may be felt not among international visitors but among Senegalese believers themselves. Senegal is approximately 95% Muslim and 0.2% evangelical. 一名塞内加尔基督徒在达喀尔青年奥林匹克运动会期间与活动志愿者分享福音. IMB 相片 当来自世界各地的运动员和观众为2026年达喀尔青年奥林匹克运动会而填满了塞内加尔的街道时,传教士和当地信徒正在祈祷这次活动将留下比奖牌和记忆更多的东西.

对在塞内加尔服务的国际传教委员会传教士卡森·韦斯特来说,奥运会是一个独特的机会,不仅可以让游客接受福音,而且可以动员当地教会在奥运会火焰被扑灭后很长一段时间里在传教中发挥更积极的作用。 “这是非洲大陆有史以来第一次举行的奥林匹克活动,”West说。

" 对于我们来说,这是一个机会,可以问:‘我们该怎么办? ' 从10月31日开始到11月13日结束的青年奥林匹克运动会正在三个主办城市举行:达喀尔、迪亚姆尼亚迪奥和萨利。 活动组织者预计有近2700名14至17岁的运动员参加35个运动会,并代表200多个代表团.

该运动会吸引了一百万观众,而西部报道有超过6000名活动志愿者为所有会场配备人员. 如此多的人聚集在塞内加尔,韦斯特和他的团队集中力量为塞内加尔的教会准备福音会的机会. West说:“我们可以跑去躲起来,或者做这件事。”

“我们决定这样做。” 2026年塞内加尔达喀尔青年奥林匹克运动会是非洲大陆首次举办的奥林匹克运动会. IMB Photo West是IMB在塞内加尔工作的团队领导,该部的工作集中在三个领域:福音参与、教会进步和社区发展。 青年奥林匹克运动会的外联自然符合前两个优先事项。

他说,“我们的做法是动员地方教会”。 这是他们的后院。 战略不是依赖大量国际志愿者的涌入,而是以装备当地信徒为中心,尽管有一个来自美国的志愿者团队在服役. 塞内加尔在大达喀尔地区有四所浸信会教堂。

许多代表会众的领导人以及其他部委伙伴参加了专门为奥运会设计的福音会培训。 塞内加尔的教会领袖和部委伙伴参加了一个福音会培训班,专门在达喀尔青年奥林匹克运动会期间分享福音。

IMB Photo A关键推广方法涉及交易纪念针,这是熟悉的奥林匹克传统. 志愿者在提供以福音为核心的材料之前,将交换作为自然对话的起步器. 每枚接针都附有一张卡片,上面有QR码,与从之前的奥运会和世界杯推广活动改编而来的数字接战平台相接.

扫描代码的访客被引导到在线资源中,可以与经过训练的数字响应器连接. 在美国有经验的志愿者正在帮助提供后续对话. 西方说, “我们正在借鉴以往奥运会有效运用的战略。

“开口福音对话是一个简单、非暗示性的方法。 交易纪念针是奥林匹克传统. 志愿者在达喀尔青年奥林匹克运动会期间利用这些针头开始福音驱动的对话. 每个接针都配有以QR代码为特色的卡片,将人与训练有素的数字响应器相接. IMB 相片 这项工作超越了达喀尔。

IMB团队和教会合作伙伴在三个东道城市各设一站. 一个由3个全球传教伙伴组成的一个IMB小组正在协助协调迪亚姆尼亚迪奥的外联工作,一个IMB小组和一个浸信会教会正在萨利组织努力。

西方认为,国际游客、塞内加尔信徒本身可能感受到最大的潜在影响。 塞内加尔穆斯林约占95%,福音派约占0.2%。 在一个269人死亡的国家d
